focus.jtag: Stocks hold gains after their best day since early August as Iran offers to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and crude slides; the scanner boarded a single Type C merger-breakout name
focus.jnote: The week’s risk-on tone carries over — but there’s exactly one thing to verify, not a table to pound. After the S&P 500 rose 1.5% Monday for its best day since Aug 4 and the Nasdaq notched its first record since June, futures held firm: S&P 500 futures ~+0.1%, Dow futures ~+0.4%, with the Nasdaq 100 around the flatline. The biggest driver: Iran reportedly offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the U.S. eases military pressure, and Saudi Aramco restarted its East-West pipeline — sending Brent below $100 for the first time since Sept 9 and WTI down ~2–3.5% toward the low-$90s. The VIX is near ~14.9, close to a year-to-date low, and lower oil knocked the 10Y down toward ~4.66%. Gold recovered above ~$4,350. The scanner boarded a single Type C name (WBD) on the Paramount merger-settlement breakout; on a calm-but-headline-driven tape, verify it hard before assuming there’s a trade.
focus.notdown: Media/M&A (WBD) and chips/AI (SMH, NVDA, AMD) are the groups with a bid — WBD ripped to a new 52-week high on Paramount merger-settlement progress, and chips are rebounding with short-covering ahead of Nvidia’s print. But be honest: WBD’s move is a deal-closing-probability reprice, not a clean trend, and chips are bid on anticipation into NVDA earnings. WBD is the one name that cleared the scanner, but it’s a zero-day-old breakout with only 1 S/R layer. Watch-only outside the one boarded name.
focus.notup: Energy & fuel-sensitive names have less to fear on the short side today with oil sliding on Hormuz-reopen hopes, so clean bear-call setups are thin — and selling bear calls into a risk-on, VIX-near-lows relief tape carries squeeze risk on any re-escalation headline. The disciplined answer on the short side is to sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why not GREEN? Two reasons. First, even though composite (42) and P(≥1% gap) (30%) both sit below their triggers, the tape faces NVDA earnings Wednesday after the close — a mega-cap chip event that can gap the whole complex — plus a headline-driven Hormuz/oil story that could reverse on any re-escalation. Second, the single boarded name (WBD, Type C · Grade B) is a same-day breakout still proving itself: enormous 10.77x volume but only 1 S/R layer (pivot $28.90, −6.3%) and a catalyst that is a merger reprice rather than a durable technical trend. That is a half-size, verify-first candidate, not a green light. Half size, A-grade only; confirm 4-VAL and liquidity at 9:35 before any entry. Cash is a position today.

setups.read: The scanner boarded WBD Type C on a same-day 52-week/all-time-high breakout; it copies through at Grade B. WBD closed ~$30.80 Monday (up ~10.8%) on huge 10.77x volume, piercing the ~$30.92 52-week high, after reports that Paramount Skydance is near a settlement with California’s AG to clear the WBD merger. Be honest about the weak spots: this is a zero-session-old breakout still proving itself — size accordingly — the catalyst is a merger deal-closing reprice rather than a durable technical trend, and there is only 1 S/R layer (the pivot ~$28.90, about −6.3%). Liquidity screened OK (ATM spread $0.02, OI 565). Next earnings ~Nov 5 is safely outside DTE.
setups.check_note: Half size at most — a same-day breakout can fade. Run 4-VAL at 9:35: price > Mon close ($30.80), > today’s open, upper third of range. Merger-headline risk cuts both ways — any deal setback gaps it down; keep the short put at/below the $28.90 pivot and confirm bid-ask ≤ $0.10 before entry.

risks: NVDA earnings (Wed after the close) — the first mega-cap chip print of the season; short-covering is already running into it. A guide either way gaps the whole AI/chip complex and can drag the tape — the week’s biggest single-stock swing factor.

Strait of Hormuz & oil — Iran’s reopen offer is single-source and unverified, contingent on the U.S. easing pressure; crude fell below $100 on the hope but any re-escalation sends oil and inflation fear vertical again. Houthi moves near Bab el-Mandeb add a second chokepoint risk.
10-year near 5% — the 10Y had touched ~5.0% and eased toward ~4.66% only on lower oil; a rate pop back through 5% hits rate-sensitive and AI/hyperscaler names hardest and would stall the relief.

WBD liquidity & 4-VAL — the one boarded name is a same-day breakout with only 1 S/R layer and a merger-headline catalyst that can gap either way. Verify the spread and 4-VAL manually at 9:35; do not enter on an unconfirmed, faded breakout.

Fed still hawkish — with the Fed flagging further tightening and inflation risk from the oil spike lingering, a re-tightening of financial conditions on any hot data or oil reversal is the macro combination to watch.
